'''Christopher Bernard Porter''' (born May 9, 1978) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. Known for his large [[afro]] hairstyle and giant [[vertical leap]], he created excitement early in his career with his [[Slam dunk|dunking]] and [[Rebound (basketball)|rebounding]] abilities. Largely seen as too undersized to play [[power forward]] at the [[NBA]] level, his style fit in perfectly with coach [[Cliff Ellis]]' style of full court pressure while playing [[college basketball]] for the [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn Tigers]].

==Early life==
Porter was born and raised in [[Abbeville, Alabama]], a small town with "just three streetlights" and a few thousand people.<ref name=nbl>{{cite web |last=Singh | first=Anendra |url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/hawkes-bay-today/news/article.cfm?c_id=1503462&objectid=11576119 |title=Basketball: Porter walks tall in NZ |work=nzherald.co.nz |date=January 19, 2016 |access-date=January 20, 2016}}</ref> He attended Abbeville High where he helped the school win the 4A State Championship as a senior. He subsequently earned 4A State Player of the Year honors.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ahsfhs.org/Basketball/POY.asp |title=ASWA Basketball Player of the Year |work=ahsfhs.org |date=February 24, 2016}}</ref>

==College career==
Between 1996 and 1998, Porter played college basketball for [[Chipola College]] where he earned [[Junior college|JUCO]] All-American honors. He then played two years for [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn University]], helping them reach the [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|NCAA Sweet Sixteen]] in 1998–99, Porter's junior season. He was named [[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] [[SEC Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Player of the Year]] that season and was selected to the [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-America]] team. The following year, Porter was pictured on the cover of ''[[Sports Illustrated]]'' as the Auburn Tigers were picked to win the national title. However, true to the [[Sports Illustrated cover jinx]], the Tigers struggled and Porter was suspended for the last eight games of the season for accepting money from an agent while still in college.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2000/02/29/sports/colleges-men-s-basketball-porter-has-admitted-agent-gave-him-money.html |title=COLLEGES: MEN'S BASKETBALL; Porter Has Admitted Agent Gave Him Money |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=February 29, 2000 |access-date=January 20, 2016}}</ref> Porter reportedly accepted $2,500 to save his mother from being evicted from her home and claimed he did not know the person was affiliated with any sports agency.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/basketball/college/news/2000/02/28/porter_agent_ap/ |title=Porter confesses; Sources say Auburn star needed money to aid mother |work=Sports Illustrated |date=February 29, 2000 |access-date=January 20, 2016 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20010713131656/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/basketball/college/news/2000/02/28/porter_agent_ap/ |archive-date=July 13, 2001 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/basketball/college/news/2000/03/12/porter_agent_ap/ |title=Loaner identified; Registered agent Walsh reportedly paid Porter $2,500 |work=Sports Illustrated |date=March 12, 2000 |access-date=January 20, 2016 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20010713134033/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/basketball/college/news/2000/03/12/porter_agent_ap/ |archive-date=July 13, 2001 }}</ref>

==Professional career==

===NBA===
Porter was selected with the 55th overall pick in the [[2000 NBA draft]] by the [[Golden State Warriors]]. As a rookie in [[2000–01 NBA season|2000–01]], he averaged 8.6 points, 3.7 rebounds and 1.2 assists in 51 games.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/p/portech01/gamelog/2001/ |title=Chris Porter 2000-01 Game Log |work=Basketball-Reference.com |access-date=January 20, 2016}}</ref> His season was hindered, however, by a nagging sprained left ankle.<ref>{{cite web|last=Wallace |first=Desmond M. |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/statitudes/news/2001/02/26/goldenstate_injuries/index.html |title=Woe is them; Injuries wreck Golden State's season |work=Sports Illustrated |date=February 27, 2001 |access-date=January 20, 2016 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20010609014515/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/statitudes/news/2001/02/26/goldenstate_injuries/index.html |archive-date=June 9, 2001 }}</ref> Despite a solid rookie season, the 2001 off-season proved to be Porter's downfall from the NBA. After showing up three days late to the Warriors' summer camp, followed by an off-the-court arrest, Porter was traded to the [[Charlotte Hornets]] in a three-team, eight-player deal on October 25, 2001, just days prior to the start of the [[2001–02 NBA season|2001–02 season]]. However, Porter missed his flight the next morning from [[Oakland, California]], which the Hornets said was enough reason to waive him on the spot. With pending drug charges against him from an August arrest in Alabama in which police stopped him and found cocaine, marijuana and a handgun in his car, the Hornets refused to give Porter any leeway.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://a.espncdn.com/nba/news/2001/1026/1269302.html |title=Charlotte waives forward Porter |work=ESPN.com |date=October 26, 2001 |access-date=January 20, 2016}}</ref> Porter would never play in the NBA after the 2000 - 2001 season with his final game being on April 18, 2001, in an 81 - 95 loss to the Vancouver Grizzlies. In his final game, Porter recorded a double-double (14 points and 11 rebounds) as the Warriors starting small forward.

===CBA, USBL, Italy and Portugal===
In January 2002, Porter signed with the [[Dakota Wizards]] of the [[Continental Basketball Association]]. In 24 games for Dakota in 2001–02, he averaged 16.4 points, 6.6 rebounds, 1.8 assists and 1.7 steals per game, helping the team win the 2002 CBA championship. Following the CBA season, he had a six-game stint with the [[Oklahoma Storm]] of the [[United States Basketball League]], helping the team win the 2002 USBL championship.

In August 2002, Porter signed with [[Fabriano Basket|Carifac Fabriano]] of the [[Lega Basket Serie A]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.legabasket.it/news/7113/carmenati_convince_anche_chris_porter |title=Carmenati convince anche Chris Porter |work=legabasket.it |date=August 3, 2002 |access-date=January 20, 2016 |language=it}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.legabasket.it/news/7679/fabriano_accoglie_chris_porter |title=Fabriano accoglie Chris Porter |work=legabasket.it |date=August 26, 2002 |access-date=January 20, 2016 |language=it}}</ref> His stint with the Italian club lasted just 10 games, averaging 12.9 points, 4.8 rebounds and 1.5 assists per game. In January 2003, he re-joined the Dakota Wizards. Later that year, he had stint in Puerto Rico with [[Gigantes de Carolina (men's basketball)|Gigantes de Carolina]] and again played for the [[Oklahoma Storm]].

For the 2003–04 season, Porter moved to Portugal where he played for [[Oliveirense (basketball)|Oliveirense Simoldes]]. His stint lasted until January 2004 when he was released by the club. He went on to play for both the Dakota Wizards and Oklahoma Storm once again during 2004. In 2004–05, he split the season playing for the Dakota Wizards and Korean team [[Daegu Orions]].

===China and Philippines===
For the 2005–06 season, Porter moved to China where he joined [[Fujian Xunxing]]. He played 10 games for Fujian before departing the club in December 2005 and joining the [[Barangay Ginebra Kings]] of the [[Philippine Basketball Association]] (PBA).<ref>{{cite web |last=Beltran |first=Nelson |url=http://www.philstar.com/sports/313225/porter-lifts-kings-over-phone-pals |title=Porter lifts Kings over Phone Pals |work=PhilStar.com |date=December 22, 2005 |access-date=January 20, 2016}}</ref> He led the team through to the semi-finals of the [[2005–06 PBA Fiesta Conference|2006 PBA Playoffs]] before they lost their series 4–3 to rival and eventual champion, the [[Red Bull Barako]].

Porter returned to China for the 2006–07 season, re-joining Fujian Xunxing. In 29 games for the club in 2006–07, he averaged 22 points and 13 rebounds per game.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fiba.com/pages/eng/fc/gameCent/p/leagueid/CHN/ot/1/pid/6023359/season/2007/tid/6025012/playerView.html |title=Christopher Bernard PORTER | Season 2006/2007 |work=FIBA.com |access-date=January 20, 2016}}{{dead link|date=September 2023|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> In January 2007, he played for the [[Chinese Basketball Association|CBA]] All-Stars in a two-game exhibition series against the [[Korean Basketball League]] All-Stars. Porter scored 17 points in Game 1,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www1.china.org.cn/sports/news/2007-01/29/content_1198072.htm |title=Basketball: S. Korea All-Stars Edge Out China |work=China.org.cn |date=January 29, 2007 |access-date=January 20, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161005230520/http://www1.china.org.cn/sports/news/2007-01/29/content_1198072.htm |archive-date=October 5, 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref> and 13 points in Game 2, with the CBA losing both games.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/news/KOR-Korean-all-stars-win-again-against-China |title=KOR - Korean all stars win again against China |work=FIBA.com |date=January 31, 2007 |access-date=January 20, 2016}}</ref> He again played for Fujian in 2007–08, but he managed just 15 games before departing the club in December 2007.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fiba.com/pages/eng/fc/gameCent/p/leagueid/CHN/ot/1/pid/6023359/season/2008/tid/6025012/tidstat//playerView.html |title=Christopher Bernard PORTER | Season 2007/2008 |work=FIBA.com |access-date=January 20, 2016 }}{{dead link|date=September 2023|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> He returned to Fujian in 2008, playing for the club until December 2010 when he was released half-way through the 2010–11 season due to an injury.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/84387/fujian-waive-chris-porter.html |title=Fujian waive Chris Porter |work=Sportando.com |date=December 17, 2010 |access-date=January 20, 2016}}</ref>

In June 2011, Porter joined the [[Powerade Tigers]] for the [[2011 PBA Governors' Cup]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ballerspinas.com/2011/06/powerade-tigers-wants-to-get-ginebras.html#.Vp8lOMB94zY |title=Powerade Tigers Want To Get Ginebra's Former Import Chris Porter To Replace John Nathan Williamson |work=BallersPinas.com |date=June 7, 2011 |access-date=January 20, 2016}}</ref>

===NBA D-League===
After a stint in the [[American Basketball Association (2000–present)|ABA]] for the [[Las Vegas Aces (ABA)|Las Vegas Aces]] in 2011–12, Porter began a successful three-year run with the [[Fort Wayne Mad Ants]] of the [[NBA Development League]] between December 2012<ref>{{cite web |url=http://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/224974/Mad-Ants-Acquire-Chris-Porter-Waive-Sean-Sonderleiter |title=Mad Ants Acquire Chris Porter, Waive Sean Sonderleiter |work=RealGM.com |date=December 12, 2012 |access-date=January 20, 2016}}</ref> and April 2015,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/chris-porter-contract-terminated-for-violating-nba-d-league-anti-drug-program/n-4947771 |title=Chris Porter Contract Terminated for Violating NBA D-League Anti-Drug Program |work=OurSportsCentral.com |date=April 6, 2015 |access-date=January 20, 2016}}</ref> winning a championship with the team in 2013–14.<ref>{{cite web |last=Rankin | first=Duane |url=http://www.montgomeryadvertiser.com/story/rankinfile/2015/04/10/former-auburn-star-porter-out-of-d-league-after-violation/25617929/ |title=Former Auburn star Chris Porter out of D-League after drug policy violation |work=MontgomeryAdvertiser.com |date=April 10, 2015 |access-date=January 20, 2016}}</ref> In 126 regular season games for the Mad Ants over three seasons, Porter averaged 6.1 points, 4.6 rebounds and 1.1 steals in 17.8 minutes per game.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/dleague/players/p/portech01d.html |title=Chris Porter D-League stats |work=Basketball-Reference.com |access-date=January 20, 2016}}</ref>

In June 2014, Porter had a one-game stint with the [[Texas Lone Star Strikers]] of the [[International Basketball League]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ibl.com/player_profile.php?playerid=1752 |title=Chris Porter Stats |work=IBL.com |access-date=January 20, 2016}}</ref>

===New Zealand===
On January 19, 2016, Porter signed with the [[Hawke's Bay Hawks]] for the [[2016 New Zealand NBL season]].<ref name="nbl" /><ref>{{cite web |last=Anderson |first=Niall |url=http://nzhoops.co.nz/former-nba-player-signs-with-hawks/ |title=Former NBA Player Signs With Hawks |work=NZhoops.co.nz |date=January 20, 2016 |access-date=January 20, 2016 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160122060351/http://nzhoops.co.nz/former-nba-player-signs-with-hawks/ |archive-date=January 22, 2016 }}</ref> Named co-captain of the team alongside [[Aidan Daly]], he made his debut for the Hawks in the team's season opener on March 13. In 26 minutes of action as a starter, he recorded a team-high 21 points and 6 rebounds in an 89–74 loss to the [[Wellington Saints]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.basketball.org.nz/News/saints-go-to-2-0 |title=SAINTS GO TO 2-0 |work=Basketball.org.nz |date=March 13, 2016 |access-date=March 13, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fibalivestats.com/u/NZN/279819/ |title=Hawks vs Saints |work=FIBALiveStats.com |date=March 13, 2016 |access-date=March 13, 2016}}</ref> On March 24, he recorded a double-double with 22 points and 10 rebounds against the [[Southland Sharks]]. Four days later, he recorded a second consecutive double-double with 23 points and 10 rebounds against the [[Canterbury Rams]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Singh | first=Anendra |url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/hawkes-bay-today/sport/news/article.cfm?c_id=1503460&objectid=11612814 |title=Basketball: Hawks fight but stumble in overtime |work=nzherald.co.nz |date=March 28, 2016 |access-date=April 4, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Singh | first=Anendra |url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/hawkes-bay-today/sport/news/article.cfm?c_id=1503460&objectid=11613160 |title=Basketball: Brave stuff but no cigar |work=nzherald.co.nz |date=March 29, 2016 |access-date=April 4, 2016}}</ref> After going 0–4 over their first four games, things got worse for the Hawks on April 3 with Porter being ruled out for the rest of the season with a hamstring injury.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/hawkes-bay-today/news/article.cfm?c_id=1503462&objectid=11616451 |title=Basketball: Triple blow for Hawks |work=nzherald.co.nz |date=April 4, 2016 |access-date=April 4, 2016}}</ref> In those four games, Porter averaged 18.3 points, 8.0 rebounds, 1.0 assists and 1.5 steals per game.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.foxsportspulse.com/team_info.cgi?action=PSTATS&pID=201332300&client=11-8336-114263-402361-25074088 |title=Player statistics for Chris Porter |work=FoxSportsPulse.com |access-date=April 4, 2016}}</ref>

==Other media==
Porter has appeared as a playable character in the video games ''[[ESPN NBA 2Night]]'', ''[[NBA 2K1]]'', ''[[NBA Hoopz]]'', ''[[NBA Live 2001]]'' (''[[PlayStation 2|PS2]]'' & ''[[Microsoft Windows|PC]]'' versions), ''[[NBA Live 2002]]'', ''[[NBA ShootOut 2001]]'' (''[[PlayStation (console)|PS1]]'' version only) and ''[[NBA ShootOut 2002]]''.{{citation needed|date=August 2023}}

==Drug arrests==
Porter has been arrested numerous times due to drug possession. The first time was in August 2001 when Alabama police found small plastic bags of cocaine and marijuana in the car he was driving.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/basketball/nba/news/2001/08/24/porter_drugchargers_ap/ |title=Porter arrested on drug charges |work=Sports Illustrated |date=August 24, 1469 |access-date=January 20, 2016 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20010828180917/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/basketball/nba/news/2001/08/24/porter_drugchargers_ap/ |archive-date=August 28, 2001 }}</ref> In April 2006, Alabama police charged him with driving under the influence and second-degree possession of marijuana.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/espn/wire?section=ncb&id=2395676 |title=Former Auburn star Chris Porter arrested |work=ESPN.com |date=April 3, 2006 |access-date=January 20, 2016}}</ref> In November 2010, he pleaded guilty in Houston County Circuit Court to a misdemeanor marijuana charge.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.al.com/sports/index.ssf/2010/11/former_auburn_basketball_star.html |title=Former Auburn basketball star Chris Porter pleads guilty to marijuana charge |work=AL.com |date=November 19, 2010 |access-date=January 20, 2016}}</ref>
In January 2021, Porter was arrested by the Dothan Police Department for 1st degree sexual abuse.  Arrest record show the charge stems from an allegation that he fondled a female teenager (18 years of age).<ref>{{cite web|last1=Riley, Sable|first1=sriley@dothaneagle.com|date=Jan 11, 2021|title=Former Auburn basketball star accused of sexual abuse|url=https://dothaneagle.com/news/local/former-auburn-basketball-star-accused-of-sexual-abuse/article_4037e160-542d-11eb-b37e-e7c5f4a26618.html|url-status=live|access-date=1 Jun 2021|website=Dothan Eagle|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210116181143/https://dothaneagle.com/news/local/former-auburn-basketball-star-accused-of-sexual-abuse/article_4037e160-542d-11eb-b37e-e7c5f4a26618.html |archive-date=January 16, 2021 }}</ref>
